entries.title: METR: independent assessment of AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic
entries.summary: METR ran a high-access evaluation at Anthropic, 12 Aug to 29 Oct 2026. It reviewed internal data on training compute, benchmarks and AI speedups. It tests whether AI accelerates AI R&D.
entries.analysis: Rare third-party verification of a lab's RSP-relevant claim.

entries.title: Zvi's AI #193: Anthropic S-1 warns it may imminently meet RSP acceleration threshold
entries.summary: Anthropic's modified S-1 says it may imminently meet the RSP definition of 'dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI'. Zvi also covers the SURA debate and the OpenAI Model Spec update.
entries.analysis: Pairs with the METR assessment above.

entries.title: Enforcing Accountable Disclosure in Confidential AI (CORDE)
entries.summary: CORDE is a system for confidential VMs. It confines user-derived data by default. Data leaves only after being 'declared': exact contents, recipient and reason go to a user-accessible record. It targets agents and provider safety monitoring.
entries.analysis: Confidential-compute audit logging; relevant to verification tooling.

entries.title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
entries.summary: The paper builds two model organisms: a narrow-trigger one that cheats by following a planted wrong hint, and a broad-trigger one fine-tuned on insecure code. It then formalizes post-hoc suppression and tests how durable it is.
entries.analysis: Useful testbeds; the durability results need a full read.

entries.title: Write Facts the Way Models Read Them: Lifting the Two-Hop Curse
entries.summary: The paper argues the two-hop failure is a writing problem, not a reasoning deficit. Fine-tuning stores a new fact as an answer to say. The second hop reads the bridge entity from middle layers. Patching that entity representation in helps.
entries.analysis: Concrete interpretability result with a causal patching test.

entries.title: An Axiomatic Framework for RL in Open Multi-Agent Systems
entries.summary: The paper derives value-function learning for n-agent ad hoc teamwork from the Shapley axioms: efficiency, symmetry and linearity. It treats the axioms as structural constraints. It uses a new decomposition of open versus fully controllable systems.
entries.analysis: Matches your top interest: theory for multi-agent settings.

entries.title: Efficient Lempel-Ziv Prediction with the Run-Length BWT
entries.summary: A PIBBSS 2026 project under Vanessa Kosoy. It cuts the runtime of Kosoy's polynomial-time algorithm for predicting repetitive sequences. The post explains the ideas informally.

entries.title: People Should Resolve Tensions In AI Safety Research
entries.summary: The post argues for short writeups that compile evidence from papers, especially contradictory evidence, and reconcile it into an answer. It says papers are an arbitrary unit and output will outgrow readers.
entries.analysis: Meta-perspective; useful for your reading workflow.

entries.title: Why would an AI pause (noticeably) hurt the economy?
entries.summary: Raemon challenges the claim that AI policy must avoid hurting the economy. He asks why a pause would hurt much, citing the 2007-2009 recession.
entries.analysis: Short discussion piece on a live pause-policy argument.

entries.title: Verified but Vacuous: Three Failure Surfaces of LLM-Driven Verified Code Generation
entries.summary: The paper argues one 'verified' number hides three properties: verifier acceptance, proof-to-spec binding, and spec fidelity. It shows the first two separate, using a Dafny pipeline reproduction under Claude Opus 4.7 on three Python benchmarks.
entries.analysis: Verification-semantics caution; transferable to treaty verification.
